prediction.likelyOutcome: U.S. Bank is very likely to obtain both foreclosure and a substantial in personam money judgment; the procedural combination of in rem and in personam relief is essentially secure given the borrower's failure to object. The live uncertainty going into the bench trial concerns the forbearance agreement's effect and any standing challenge, plus how much of the pleaded $46,290,900.25 (versus a reduced, forbearance- or fair-value-adjusted figure) is actually proven and collectible.

issues.label: Core Liability on the Note/Mortgage Default
Propriety of Combined In Rem/In Personam Pleading
Additional Accrued Interest, Fees, and Costs Beyond the Pleaded Figure

outcome.description: After a bench trial the district court held Penn Realty breached the loan agreement and entered an in personam money judgment for U.S. Bank of $51,392,086.96 (no judgment in mortgage foreclosure was entered); the Third Circuit affirmed that judgment in a separate unpublished opinion (No. 23-2185, Sept. 25, 2024). In this precedential appeal the Third Circuit upheld the subsequent execution sale of the apartment building under Fed. R. Civ. P. 69(a) and affirmed the denial of the borrower's motion to quash.
